title: SAE (sparse autoencoder) interpretability plan — DEFERRED, for later
status: NOT the current path. The active work is CODEBOOKS for the WP2-axis annotation. This is filed for later.
which_paper: This belongs to the PREGNANCY-REPRESENTATION / 'what do fetal-ultrasound foundation models encode' paper, NOT to the WP2 annotation. Do not mix the two: WP2 annotation wants PROPORTIONS OF COARSE APPEARANCE CLASSES (1-of-K partitioning is right for that, and K=16 sits inside the ~32-concept human ceiling from Ramaswamy CVPR 2023). SAEs answer a different question: what NAMEABLE CONCEPTS exist.
why_sae_over_vq: The analytic argument: a 1-of-K code provably cannot name any concept present in more than 1/K of patches, and cannot express a patch containing SEVERAL concepts at once (tissue type + depth artefact + boundary + gain). An ultrasound patch plausibly does. A sparse mixture can; a hard assignment cannot.
headline: Switch the interpretability layer from VQ to a TopK sparse autoencoder (M=4096, k=16) on ONE pre-registered FetalCLIP layer, keep VQ K=320 as the matched-capacity baseline, and gate every named feature on a random-weight-encoder control — because a 1-of-K code provably cannot name any concept more common than 1/K of patches.
protocol:
INPUTS (all already on disk, no re-extraction of the trained encoder): FetalCLIP ViT-L/14 patch tokens, 20,413 IMPACT frames / 908 fetuses, 16x16=256 patches/frame, 1024-d = 5.2M patch rows.

FIXED BEFORE ANY OUTCOME OR GA NUMBER IS COMPUTED:
1. LAYER. One layer only, chosen from the project's existing layer-Shapley result for the GA clock, then frozen. Do NOT concatenate layers: simulated at 12 layers x 64-d, best-single-unit concept AUC was 0.551 (last layer alone), 0.556 (mid layer alone), 0.549 (12-layer concat), 0.549 (concat with per-layer drift removed) - concatenation buys nothing and its atoms spend 0.20-0.23 of their norm in one dominant layer vs 0.083 at chance, i.e. atoms index LAYER IDENTITY, an artefact that will look like a finding.
2. ARCHITECTURE. TopK SAE (Gao et al. 2406.04093): TopK sets sparsity directly, removing the L1-coefficient sweep, and its auxiliary loss keeps dead latents low at scale. Fallback if per-patch k proves too rigid: BatchTopK (2412.06410). NOT L1/ReLU (Paulo et al. show it is more seed-stable but shrinkage-biased; Chaudhry 2605.05341 characterises L1 feature starvation as an optimisation-geometry pathology).
3. GRID. M = 4096 (4x expansion on 1024-d) and k = 16. ONE grid point. Any deviation is a new construction and pays the multiplicity cost in step 12.
4. PREPROCESSING. Per-layer token standardisation, then subtract the per-frame token mean (this is the drift term that produced layer-identity atoms in simulation).
5. DEAD FEATURES. Gao auxiliary loss (reconstruct residual from top-k_aux dead latents). Report alive fraction explicitly - this project already saw a gradient VQ codebook collapse to 9/32 codes, so aliveness is measured, never assumed.
6. SEEDS. 3. A feature is REPORTABLE only if it replicates across all 3 at cosine >= 0.7 on its per-frame activation profile. Justification: Paulo et al. 2501.16615 found only ~30% feature overlap between seeds in a 131k-latent SAE, with TopK MORE seed-dependent than L1.
7. SPLITS. GroupKFold by fetus, 5 folds. The SAE is fitted inside training folds only.

CONTROL ARMS - run at the same time, same frames, same M/k/seeds/folds, same naming pipeline. These are the denominator of every reported number, not an appendix:
8a. RANDOM-WEIGHT ENCODER. Re-initialise FetalCLIP by sampling per-matrix Gaussians matched to each trained matrix's mean and variance (Heap's 're-randomised' scheme - NOT naive default init, which their L1-norm result shows is a weaker null because parameter norms drift from the trained model). One extra extraction pass over 20,413 frames (<1h).
8b. SHUFFLED-INPUT. Trained encoder, patch tokens spatially permuted within each frame. Kills anatomy, preserves marginal token statistics.
8c. CROSS-ENCODER REPLICATION. A feature named on FetalCLIP must have a counterpart on USF-MAE or USFM (cosine >= 0.5 between per-frame activation profiles). Necessary but NOT sufficient - this project's own mimic-effect result showed cross-stream agreement reaching Mantel r=0.70 between streams independent by construction. Dispositive only jointly with 8a.
8d. DOMAIN-vs-NATURAL-IMAGE CONTRAST. DINOv2 ViT-g is natural-image-trained; the other three are ultrasound. Le et al. 2407.10785 established this control in pathology (SAE dims on a pathology FM hit rho=0.70 with plasma-cell counts, an ImageNet-DINO ViT-S of matched design did not). Directional prediction, stated in advance, allowed to fail.

EXECUTION:
9. Fit the SAE (3 seeds) on train-fold patches. Record explained variance, alive-feature fraction, mean L0. Then fit the identical SAE on arms 8a and 8b.
10. Per-frame feature profile: max-pool AND mean-pool over patches. Both pre-specified; counted as 2 poolings in multiplicity.
11. NAMING. For each replicated feature take its top-64 activating patches (held-out folds only), render them with their in-frame spatial location, and record three quantities: (i) spatial coherence - do top patches occupy a consistent anatomical location; (ii) plane specificity - distribution of the 3 coarse plane labels among top patches; (iii) depth/gain confound - mean normalised patch depth and mean patch intensity of top patches vs the dataset marginal. A feature explained by depth or intensity alone is NAMED as an acquisition-physics feature. That is a legitimate reportable finding about what these encoders encode, not a failure.
12. ABSTRACTNESS (Heap's only working separator). Compute the entropy of each feature's activation distribution over (a) patch spatial position and (b) coarse plane, for trained / random-weight / shuffled arms. In Heap et al. it was activation-distribution entropy over token IDs - NOT any interpretability score - that separated trained from random, rising with depth in the trained model and concentrating on one or a few IDs in the random one. Report all three distributions.
13. OUTCOME-FACING EVALUATION, ONCE, AT THE END. Per-fetus pooled feature profile -> GroupKFold ridge/logistic against GA (continuous), birth percentile, <p10, >p90, and PE as maternal negative control. Compare against the VQ K=320 per-fetus histogram at matched capacity. Paired bootstrap, 2000 resamples, on the DIFFERENCE. Outcome labels are evaluation-only and never model inputs.
14. CONFOUND ADJUSTMENT on every reported association: plane, GA, scanner/dataset, per-fetus image count.

PRE-REGISTERED NUMERIC BARS (simulated, in track1_vq_vs_sae_measurements.csv):
- Naming bar, n=908, M=4096: a feature-to-variable |r| must exceed 0.145 (95th pct of the label-permutation max-statistic over M features); 0.155 at the 99th. Same quantity at M=320/1024/16384 = 0.129/0.131/0.154; at n=544 (clinical) = 0.158/0.175/0.187/0.196. Feature redundancy (rank-64 shared structure) shifted these by <0.005, so the bar is set by M and n alone.
- 'SAE beats VQ' bar: paired-bootstrap resolution at n=908 near r=0.615 means the CI on a difference excludes 0 only at |delta r| >~ 0.065 (simulated at residual correlation 0.9: delta=0.067 -> CI [+0.046,+0.088]; delta=0.002 -> [-0.018,+0.020]). So the SAE must reach per-fetus r >= 0.68, not 0.63.
- Random-encoder margin: trained-minus-random gap in best-single-unit AUC must exceed 0.05 per named feature. Deliberately set above my own simulation's concept-aligned-encoder gap of +0.026, i.e. a threshold a weakly-aligned encoder would fail.

BASELINES THAT MUST BE RUN ALONGSIDE (cheap, CPU): PCA-64 and ICA-32 on the same tokens. In the co-occurrence simulation PCA-64 reached best-single-unit AUC 0.866 and ICA-32 0.930 vs the sparse dictionary's 0.654 - ICA is flattered there because the toy's attributes are literally independent sources, but if PCA names our concepts as well as the SAE does, the SAE has not earned the switch. Do not build on ICA (user has ruled it out for the tabular latent).

THE_CONTROL_THAT_DECIDES_EVERYTHING.finding: SAEs produce interpretable-LOOKING features even from RANDOMLY-INITIALISED networks. The agent reproduced it in simulation: a random-weight encoder plus a sparse dictionary reached best-single-unit tissue AUC 0.541, against 0.567 for a concept-aligned encoder.
THE_CONTROL_THAT_DECIDES_EVERYTHING.consequence: Top-activating-patch grids are NOT evidence. Any excitement from them must be discounted to ZERO until the random-weight arm is in hand. The agent's own stated prior: P(features will look interpretable) ~= 0.95, carrying almost no information.
THE_CONTROL_THAT_DECIDES_EVERYTHING.correct_null: Heap's RE-RANDOMISED scheme — resample per-matrix Gaussians matched to each trained matrix's mean and variance. NOT naive default init, which is a weaker null because parameter norms drift from the trained model.

fixed_design_choices.architecture: TopK SAE (Gao et al. arXiv:2406.04093) — sets sparsity directly, no L1-coefficient sweep, auxiliary loss keeps dead latents low. Fallback BatchTopK (arXiv:2412.06410). NOT L1/ReLU (shrinkage-biased).
fixed_design_choices.grid: M=4096 (4x expansion on 1024-d), k=16. ONE grid point — any deviation is a new construction and pays multiplicity.
fixed_design_choices.layer: ONE layer only, chosen from the existing layer-Shapley result, then frozen. DO NOT CONCATENATE LAYERS: simulated best-single-unit concept AUC was 0.551 last-layer / 0.556 mid-layer / 0.549 12-layer concat — concatenation buys NOTHING and its atoms spend 0.20-0.23 of their norm in one dominant layer vs 0.083 at chance, i.e. the atoms index LAYER IDENTITY, an artefact that will look like a finding.
fixed_design_choices.preprocessing: per-layer token standardisation, then subtract the per-frame token mean (that drift term is what produced layer-identity atoms).
fixed_design_choices.seeds: 3. A feature is REPORTABLE only if it replicates across all 3 at cosine >=0.7 on its per-frame activation profile. Paulo & Belrose (arXiv:2501.16615) found only ~30% feature overlap between seeds at 131k latents, with TopK MORE seed-dependent than L1.
fixed_design_choices.splits: GroupKFold by fetus, 5 folds; SAE fitted inside training folds only.
fixed_design_choices.aliveness: Gao auxiliary loss; report alive fraction explicitly — this project already saw a gradient VQ codebook collapse to 9/32 codes, so aliveness is measured, never assumed.

control_arms_run_simultaneously: 8a RANDOM-WEIGHT ENCODER (re-randomised, matched per-matrix moments) — the dispositive arm. ~1h extra extraction.
8b SHUFFLED-INPUT — trained encoder, patch tokens spatially permuted within frame: kills anatomy, preserves marginal token statistics.

8c CROSS-ENCODER REPLICATION — a FetalCLIP feature needs a counterpart on USF-MAE or USFM (cosine >=0.5). NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: this project's mimic effect reached Mantel r=0.70 between streams independent by construction. Dispositive only JOINTLY with 8a.

8d DOMAIN-vs-NATURAL-IMAGE CONTRAST — DINOv2 ViT-g is natural-image-trained, the other three ultrasound. Precedent: Le et al. arXiv:2407.10785 in pathology. Directional prediction stated in advance, allowed to fail.
expected_outcome:
Stated as calibrated priors, and two of them are deflationary.

1. SAE features will look interpretable: ~0.95, and this carries almost no information. It is Heap et al.'s central finding and my own simulation reproduced it (random-weight encoder plus sparse dictionary reached best-single-unit tissue AUC 0.541, against 0.567 for a concept-aligned encoder). Any excitement generated by top-activating-patch grids should be discounted to zero until the random arm is in hand.

2. >= 10 features survive the 3-seed replication filter: ~0.8. Replication across seeds is a weaker test than it feels - correlated features replicate for uninteresting reasons.

3. The trained-minus-random gap exceeds 0.05 for >= 10 features: ~0.5. This is the genuine coin-flip of the track and the number I most expect to disappoint. Note my simulated concept-aligned encoder cleared only +0.026, i.e. below the bar I am setting - I chose a threshold that a weakly-aligned encoder would fail, on purpose.

4. A MAJORITY of high-activation features turn out to be acquisition physics - depth, attenuation, gain, cone edge, caliper overlay - rather than anatomy: ~0.7. Three project-internal facts point this way: the USF-MAE reconstruction-error confound (background and cone edges reconstruct poorly, fetal tissue well), plane eta2 reaching 0.78 in the topic analysis, and 95% of the GA correlation surviving plane residualisation (GA is real but not plane-driven, which leaves plenty of room for plane and physics to dominate variance). This is the outcome I actually expect, and it is a GOOD paper: 'these frozen fetal-ultrasound encoders spend most of their sparse capacity on acquisition physics and imaging plane, with a minority of features tracking anatomy' is a defensible, controlled characterisation of what fetal-ultrasound foundation models encode. It is a better paper than a claimed set of anatomy axes that a random encoder also produces.

5. The SAE beats VQ K=320 on per-fetus GA at r >= 0.68: ~0.25, i.e. I predict it will NOT. The VQ histogram at 0.615 is already near the frozen-feature per-fetus ceiling, and this project established that GA is DISTRIBUTED across the vocabulary (1 code 0.125, 3 -> 0.213, 10 -> 0.246, 20 -> 0.271, all 320 -> 0.385) rather than concentrated. A sparser code has no mechanism to recover more of a distributed signal, and Kantamneni et al. found SAE latents only occasionally beat baselines on downstream probing with no reliable ensemble gain. If a prediction win is reported, treat it as a multiplicity artefact until it survives the adjusted bar.

6. NET: I expect the track to yield a defensible interpretability instrument with a modest number of genuinely encoder-specific features, a large acquisition-physics fraction that must be reported as such, and no prediction improvement. Probability the whole track ends in the pre-registered kill: ~0.3 - and that outcome is still worth writing up.
kill_criterion:
Kill the SAE track and keep VQ as the project's interpretability layer if ANY ONE of the following holds at the pre-registered M=4096 / k=16:

1. Fewer than 10 features replicate across all 3 seeds at min-pairwise cosine >= 0.7 on the per-frame activation profile.
2. The trained-minus-random gap in best-single-unit AUC exceeds 0.05 for fewer than 10 replicated features (random arm = FetalCLIP re-randomised with per-matrix mean/variance matched to the trained weights, same frames, same M/k/seeds/folds, same naming pipeline).
3. The abstractness distributions - entropy of feature activation over patch spatial position and over coarse plane - are statistically indistinguishable between the trained and random-weight arms (KS test, alpha=0.01). This is Heap et al.'s only working separator failing, and it means we cannot claim our features reflect anything the encoders learned about fetal ultrasound.
4. Alive-feature fraction < 0.25 of M on held-out patches (the dictionary is effectively far smaller than reported, per Michaud et al.'s feature-manifold pathology).

On a kill, the reportable result is a strong negative: 'a sparse dictionary over frozen fetal-ultrasound encoder tokens does not yield features distinguishable from those obtainable from a random-weight encoder of identical architecture.' Given how rarely the SAE literature runs this control at all, that is a genuine contribution and it should be written up, not shelved.

NOTE - what does NOT kill the track: failing to beat VQ on GA or on any outcome. That is the EXPECTED result (see expected_outcome) and it does not bear on the interpretability claim. Conversely, a prediction win alone does not save the track if controls 1-4 fail.

failure_modes.mode: Random-net interpretability illusion - SAE features look nameable but a random-weight encoder of identical architecture yields equally nameable ones (Heap et al.; reproduced at our geometry, where a random 256->768 ReLU layer plus a sparse dictionary gave best-single-unit tissue AUC 0.523/0.541/0.541 at M=128/512/2048 against 0.567 for a concept-aligned encoder, a gap of only +0.026).
failure_modes.diagnostic: Trained-minus-random gap in best-single-unit AUC per named feature, computed on held-out folds with the matched-variance re-randomised FetalCLIP. PASS: gap > 0.05 for at least 10 replicated features. KILL: fewer than 10 clear it. Secondary, from Heap's own separator: KS test comparing the spatial-position and plane activation-entropy distributions of trained vs random features - KILL if indistinguishable at alpha=0.01.

failure_modes.mode: Acquisition physics masquerading as anatomy - features fire on depth, attenuation, gain, cone edge or caliper overlay rather than tissue. The project has already hit exactly this with USF-MAE reconstruction error (background and cone edges reconstruct poorly, fetal tissue well) and with plane eta2 reaching 0.78 in the topic analysis.
failure_modes.diagnostic: For each feature's top-64 patches: mean normalised in-cone depth and mean patch intensity vs the dataset marginal, plus the 3-class plane distribution. CLASSIFY as acquisition-physics (a reportable finding, not a failure) if |standardised depth difference| > 1.0 SD or |intensity difference| > 1.0 SD or max plane fraction > 0.80. The reported headline must state the anatomy/physics split explicitly; a paper claiming anatomy axes while >70% of high-activation features are physics is misreported.

failure_modes.mode: Seed instability - the named feature set is an artefact of initialisation (Paulo et al.: only ~30% feature overlap across seeds at 131k latents, with TopK worse than L1).
failure_modes.diagnostic: Cosine similarity of per-frame activation profiles across the 3 seeds, greedily matched. PASS: >= 10 features with min-pairwise cosine >= 0.7 across all 3 seeds. Report the full replication-rate curve. Any feature below 0.7 is not reported, regardless of how good its exemplars look.

failure_modes.mode: Feature absorption / splitting in a hierarchical anatomy (Chanin et al.) - a 'skull' feature stops firing on cortical-bone patches because a child feature absorbed it, so the parent feature's name is false on exactly the patches that most exemplify it.
failure_modes.diagnostic: For every pair of features (parent p, child c) whose top-patch sets overlap by > 20%: the parent's firing rate on child-positive patches divided by its firing rate on child-negative patches within the same coarse plane. ABSORPTION FLAG if this ratio < 0.5. If > 20% of reported features are flagged, escalate to a Matryoshka SAE (2503.17547) - which is a pre-specified escalation, not a new construction.

failure_modes.mode: Dead / ultra-sparse features - the dictionary is nominally 4096 but effectively far smaller, so reported 'coverage' is fictional. Michaud et al. predict exactly this in manifold-like data, and Le et al. measured 88% ultra-sparse features when training on a single narrow cohort vs 20% on a diverse one - IMPACT is narrow (GA 26.0-39.3wk, SD 1.36).
failure_modes.diagnostic: Alive fraction (feature fires on >= 0.01% of held-out patches) and ultra-sparse fraction (fires on < 0.1% of frames). PASS: alive >= 0.50 of M. KILL the M=4096 grid point and report the effective dictionary size if alive < 0.25. This must be reported for the trained, random and shuffled arms alike.

failure_modes.mode: Max-statistic multiplicity - the best of 4096 features correlates with an eval variable by chance. Simulated null max |r| at n=908 rises from 0.129 (M=320) to 0.154 (M=16384), and at n=544 from 0.158 to 0.196.
failure_modes.diagnostic: Label-permutation max-statistic over ALL M features (>= 2000 permutations, permuting at the FETUS level). A feature-to-variable |r| is reportable only above 0.145 (n=908, M=4096, 95th pct) or 0.155 (99th pct). Never report a per-feature p-value.

failure_modes.mode: Leakage via fetus grouping or GA reintroduction - the SAE is fitted on all patches including test-fold fetuses, or a per-frame pooling silently reintroduces GA (e.g. image count per fetus correlating with GA).
failure_modes.diagnostic: Assert zero fetus_id intersection between train and test in every fold, and refit the SAE inside training folds only. Then: does the per-fetus feature profile predict fetus IDENTITY across folds better than chance (it must not, by construction of the split), and is the residual GA correlation after adjusting for per-fetus image count within 0.02 of the unadjusted value? Any fetus appearing in both sides of a fold is an automatic invalidation of the run, not a caveat.

failure_modes.mode: Layer-identity atoms - fitting on the layer concatenation yields atoms that index which layer they came from rather than any concept (simulated: median atom layer-concentration 0.20-0.23 vs 0.083 at chance, with concatenation giving concept AUC 0.549 vs 0.551-0.556 for a single layer).
failure_modes.diagnostic: Not applicable if the protocol is followed (one layer only). If concatenation is ever attempted: fraction of an atom's squared norm in its single dominant layer. KILL the concatenation variant if median concentration > 2x the 1/L chance value.

failure_modes.mode: Mimic effect on the cross-encoder control - two encoders agree because imaging plane is a shared confound, not because the feature is real. This project measured Mantel r=0.70 between streams that were independent BY CONSTRUCTION.
failure_modes.diagnostic: Cross-encoder agreement must be computed WITHIN plane strata and after residualising on GA, scanner and dataset. PASS only if within-stratum cross-encoder cosine >= 0.5 AND the random-weight arm's cross-encoder agreement is at least 0.2 lower. Cross-encoder agreement alone is never sufficient evidence.

failure_modes.mode: Circularity - selecting the layer, M, k, or the feature set using the outcome or GA it is then tested against.
failure_modes.diagnostic: The layer comes from the pre-existing layer-Shapley result and is written down before extraction; M=4096 and k=16 are single values; features are filtered ONLY by seed replication and the random-encoder gap, both outcome-blind. Audit check: the git commit fixing the config must predate the first outcome-facing computation. If any outcome number was seen before the config was frozen, the run is exploratory and must be reported as such.

key_papers.citation: Heap T, Lawson T, Farnik L, Aitchison L. Automated Interpretability Metrics Do Not Distinguish Trained and Random Transformers. arXiv 2501.17727v2 (Jan 2026).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: THE decisive adversarial paper, read in full. TopK SAEs (expansion 64, k=32) on Pythia 70M-6.9B: on Pythia-6.9b fuzzing AUROC was trained 0.79, randomised-excl-embeddings 0.87, step-0 0.88, randomised-incl-embeddings 0.87, and only the Gaussian-embedding negative control fell to 0.50 - the random variants did not merely match the trained model, they scored HIGHER. Explained variance, cosine similarity and L1 norm behave the same way, and the trained-vs-random gap NARROWS with model scale (bad news for a large frozen encoder). The one separator that worked was not an interpretability score: the entropy of a latent's activation distribution over token IDs ('abstractness'), which rises with depth in the trained model and concentrates on one or a few IDs in the random one. Their explicit recommendation - routine randomised baselines plus targeted abstractness measures - is adopted verbatim as arms 8a and step 12. Their randomisation scheme detail matters: match per-matrix mean and variance to the TRAINED weights, because naive init has different parameter norms and is a weaker null.

key_papers.citation: Gao L, la Tour TD, Tillman H, Goh G, Troll R, Radford A, Sutskever I, Leike J, Wu J. Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders. arXiv 2406.04093 (Jun 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The architecture we adopt. k-sparse (TopK) autoencoders control sparsity directly, removing the reconstruction/sparsity balancing act and the L1-coefficient sweep; their modifications yield few dead latents even at the largest scales tried, and they establish clean scaling laws in dictionary size and sparsity. This is what lets us pre-register a single (M, k) grid point instead of sweeping.

key_papers.citation: Le NM, et al. Learning biologically relevant features in a pathology foundation model using sparse autoencoders. arXiv 2407.10785v3 (Jul 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The closest medical-imaging precedent AND the domain-specificity control (arm 8d). SAEs on frozen PLUTO ViT-S embeddings gave dimensions correlating with cell-type counts (plasma cells rho=0.70, lymphocytes 0.63, macrophages 0.38, cancer cells 0.37, fibroblasts 0.21), while an ImageNet-DINO ViT-S of MATCHED design gave weak correlations - the trained-vs-natural-image contrast we can run with DINOv2 ViT-g. Also supplies the monosemanticity metric we reuse (entropy of the normalised |rho| distribution across candidate concepts: SAE-1736 S=0.42 vs raw PLUTO dim-148 S=0.65, max 0.70), the finding that raw encoder dimensions are polysemantic by visual inspection, and the practical lesson that training-set DIVERSITY controls ultra-sparse features (88% of features ultra-sparse when trained on one cohort vs 20% on the diverse 1M set) - directly relevant to our narrow-GA IMPACT vs wide-GA clinical choice.

key_papers.citation: Paulo G, Belrose N, et al. Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features. arXiv 2501.16615v2 (Jan 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Why we require 3-seed replication. In a 131k-latent SAE on a Llama-3-8B feedforward layer only ~30% of features were shared across seeds differing ONLY in initialisation; the effect held across multiple layers, three LLMs, two datasets and several architectures - and TopK (our choice) was MORE seed-dependent than L1 even at matched sparsity. Sets the honest framing: an SAE dictionary is a pragmatically useful decomposition, not the model's canonical feature set.

key_papers.citation: Leask P, et al. Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis. arXiv 2502.04878 (Feb 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Kills the strong claim before we make it. SAE stitching shows dictionaries are INCOMPLETE (latents from a larger SAE add novel information to a smaller one) and meta-SAEs show latents are NOT ATOMIC (they decompose further). So 'we found the vocabulary of fetal ultrasound' is not a claim this method can support; 'we found a useful, controlled decomposition' is.

key_papers.citation: Chanin D, et al. A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders. arXiv 2409.14507v6 (Sep 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The specific failure mode our anatomy hierarchy invites. When true features are hierarchical (head > skull > cortical bone, exactly our situation), sparsity pressure makes a seemingly monosemantic parent feature FAIL TO FIRE where it should because a child feature absorbs it - and varying SAE size or sparsity does not fix it. Supplies the absorption metric and forces us to test parent features on child-positive patches specifically.

key_papers.citation: Bussmann B, Leask P, Nanda N. Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders. arXiv 2503.17547 (Mar 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The pre-specified escalation if absorption bites. Nested dictionaries of increasing size, with smaller ones forced to reconstruct independently, organise features hierarchically - small dictionaries take general concepts, large ones specifics, without incentive to absorb the high-level features. Karvonen's SAEBench independently finds Matryoshka slightly worse on proxy metrics but substantially better on feature DISENTANGLEMENT, with the advantage growing with scale - and disentanglement is what we want.

key_papers.citation: Karvonen A, et al. SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability. arXiv 2503.09532v4 (Mar 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Direct warning against our natural temptation to tune on reconstruction/sparsity proxies: across 200+ SAEs and 8 architectures, gains on unsupervised proxy metrics do NOT reliably translate into better practical performance. This is why our pre-registered endpoint is nameability-under-control, not explained variance.

key_papers.citation: Engels J, Riggs S, Tegmark M. Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders. arXiv 2410.14670v2 (Oct 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: A sobering bound on how much an SAE explains: about half the error vector and >90% of its NORM is linearly predictable from the input activation, and larger SAEs mostly fail on the same contexts as smaller ones. So reconstruction quality overstates explanatory success, and scaling M is not a way out.

key_papers.citation: Stevens S, et al. Interpretable and Testable Vision Features via Sparse Autoencoders. arXiv 2502.06755v2 (Feb 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The vision-ViT recipe closest to ours: a single SAE on FROZEN ViT activations, each feature carrying real-image exemplars for meaning plus a decoding vector for causal patch-level edits, without retraining the ViT or task heads. Also reports that different pre-training objectives yield measurably different semantic abstractions - which is the comparison our four frozen encoders make possible.

key_papers.citation: Lim H, et al. Sparse autoencoders reveal selective remapping of visual concepts during adaptation (PatchSAE). arXiv 2412.05276v2 (Dec 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The concrete PATCH-level SAE framework for a CLIP ViT with patch-wise spatial attribution - our FetalCLIP is a CLIP-family ViT and our unit is the patch, so this is the nearest architectural template for step 11's spatial-coherence naming.

key_papers.citation: Pach M, et al. Sparse Autoencoders Learn Monosemantic Features in Vision-Language Models. arXiv 2504.02821v3 (Apr 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Evidence on the dictionary-size question for VISION specifically: sparsity and WIDE latents were the most influential factors for neuron-level monosemanticity in CLIP, validated against a human-perception benchmark from a large user study. Supports 4x expansion as a floor rather than a ceiling, and supplies a monosemanticity evaluation framework for vision rather than text.

key_papers.citation: Wesp P, et al. Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Medical Image Representation Learning. arXiv 2603.23794 (Mar 2026).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The medical-imaging feasibility number at our scale: SAEs on BiomedParse and DINOv3 embeddings over 909,873 CT/MRI slices reconstructed embeddings at R2 up to 0.941 and recovered up to 87.8% of downstream performance from only 10 features (99.4% dimensionality reduction), with LLM-based auto-interpretation of concepts. Establishes that both a biomedical and a general-purpose vision FM support this - which is why our domain-specificity control (8d) is a real test rather than a foregone conclusion.

key_papers.citation: Rao S, et al. Discover-then-Name: Task-Agnostic Concept Bottlenecks via Automated Concept Discovery (DN-CBM). arXiv 2407.14499v2 (Jul 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The resolution of our concept-label problem. Classical CBMs need a concept vocabulary chosen in advance - which we do not have (3 coarse plane labels, kNN-propagated, audited unreliable on clinical at 3 of 6 wrong at conf=1.00; no brain-subplane labels anywhere). DN-CBM inverts it: discover concepts with an SAE first, THEN name them and fit linear probes. FetalCLIP has a text tower, making this a viable optional follow-on.

key_papers.citation: Koh PW, Nguyen T, Tang YS, Mussmann S, Pierson E, Kim B, Liang P. Concept Bottleneck Models. arXiv 2007.04612v3 / ICML 2020.
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The comparator we must rule out and why: CBMs give nameable axes by construction, but only the axes you supplied. Not available to us for lack of a trustworthy concept vocabulary.

key_papers.citation: Mahinpei A, Clark J, Lage I, Doshi-Velez F, Pan W. Promises and Pitfalls of Black-Box Concept Learning Models. arXiv 2106.13314 (Jun 2021).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Concept leakage: soft/joint concept bottlenecks encode information beyond the named concepts, so downstream performance does not certify that the named concepts are what the model uses. A second reason not to route our interpretability claim through a CBM.

key_papers.citation: Chen C, Li O, Tao C, Barnett AJ, Su J, Rudin C. This Looks Like That: Deep Learning for Interpretable Image Recognition. arXiv 1806.10574v5 / NeurIPS 2019.
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The ProtoPNet lineage: nameable CASES rather than nameable axes. Excluded here because it requires supervised training on an outcome, and fine-tuning on GA then studying GA structure is circular by this project's own rule.

key_papers.citation: Nauta M, van Bree R, Seifert C. This Looks Like That, Because ... Explaining Prototypes for Interpretable Image Recognition. arXiv 2011.02863v2 (Nov 2020).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The prototype failure mode translated to ultrasound: prototype similarity is frequently driven by colour hue, shape, texture, contrast and saturation rather than the intended anatomical part - i.e. in our images, GAIN and DEPTH. Same confound our own USF-MAE reconstruction-error work already hit, and the reason step 11 measures patch depth and intensity explicitly.

key_papers.citation: Geirhos R, Zimmermann RS, Bilodeau B, Brendel W, Kim B. Don't trust your eyes: on the (un)reliability of feature visualizations. arXiv 2306.04719v6 (Jun 2023).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The general warning that grounds our refusal to accept exemplar panels as evidence: feature visualisations can be made to show arbitrary patterns disconnected from a network's behaviour on natural input, and they are processed differently from standard input even in unmanipulated networks. Top-activating-patch grids are persuasive and are not proof.

key_papers.citation: van den Oord A, Vinyals O, Kavukcuoglu K. Neural Discrete Representation Learning. arXiv 1711.00937v2 (Nov 2017).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The VQ-VAE baseline we are keeping, for what it is genuinely good at (discrete compression), against which the SAE's per-fetus GA performance is compared at matched capacity.

key_papers.citation: Tamkin A, Taufeeque M, Goodman ND. Codebook Features: Sparse and Discrete Interpretability for Neural Networks. arXiv 2310.17230 (Oct 2023).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The strongest defence of codebooks in mech-interp, and it concedes our point: their hidden state is the SUM OF A SMALL NUMBER of discrete codes, not one code - i.e. even the codebook-interpretability literature moved to k>1. It also requires FINETUNING the network with VQ bottlenecks, which our frozen-encoder rule forbids. Together: the case for k-sparse over 1-of-K, from inside the codebook camp.

key_papers.citation: Lee DD, Seung HS. Learning the parts of objects by non-negative matrix factorization. Nature 401:788-791 (1999).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The origin of the parts-based-naming intuition for non-negative dictionaries - and the method whose per-fetus form is already a SETTLED NULL in this project, which is why NMF is a comparator here and not a candidate.

key_papers.citation: Bussmann B, Leask P, Nanda N. BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders. arXiv 2412.06410 (Dec 2024).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The pre-specified fallback if a fixed per-patch k=16 is too rigid for ultrasound patches of very different content (background vs dense tissue): relaxing top-k to the batch level adaptively allocates more or fewer latents per sample, improving reconstruction at the same average sparsity, with average L0 directly specifiable rather than tuned.

key_papers.citation: Kantamneni S, Engels J, Rajamanoharan S, Tegmark M, Nanda N. Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing. arXiv 2502.16681 (Feb 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The deflationary result that keeps our expected_outcome honest. Across data scarcity, class imbalance, label noise and covariate shift, SAE latents only occasionally beat baselines and no ensemble reliably did - so SAEs should be adopted for INTERPRETABILITY, not on a promise of downstream gains. Squarely supports my ~0.25 prior that the SAE will not beat the VQ histogram on GA.

key_papers.citation: Thasarathan H, Forsyth J, Fel T, Kowal M, Derpanis K. Universal Sparse Autoencoders: Interpretable Cross-Model Concept Alignment. arXiv 2502.03714v2 (Feb 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: The principled version of our cross-encoder control (8c): a single overcomplete SAE that ingests activations from any of several models and decodes to any other, learning a shared concept space across vision models. Note the caution - a universal dictionary makes the mimic effect EASIER, not harder, since a shared confound like imaging plane is exactly what a universal space would capture; use it only after 8a has passed.

key_papers.citation: Michaud EJ, et al. Understanding sparse autoencoder scaling in the presence of feature manifolds. arXiv 2509.02565v2 (Sep 2025).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Directly relevant to our data: multi-dimensional 'feature manifolds' can put SAEs in a pathological regime where they learn far FEWER features in the data than there are latents in the dictionary. Fetal biometry is continuous and manifold-like (GA, size, depth), so this is our expected regime - it predicts a low alive-feature fraction and justifies making that a measured, reported quantity rather than an assumption.

key_papers.citation: Bal MA, et al. From Geometric Recovery to Causal Validation: A Reproducible Audit of Sparse Autoencoder Features. arXiv 2607.12166 (Jul 2026).
key_papers.what_it_gives_us: Shows correlational recovery and causal behaviour are different claims: up to 77% of features passing a cosine >= 0.90 recovery bar in a degraded SAE, and 9% in a well-trained one, were CAUSALLY INERT - the matched atom never fires when the feature is present, including at cosine ~1.000. Our naming step is correlational by necessity (frozen encoders, no downstream head to ablate), so this bounds what we may claim: 'this feature tracks X', never 'the encoder uses this feature to compute X'.

multiplicity:
CONSTRUCTIONS, counted honestly and kept deliberately small.

Pre-registered primary: 1 encoder (FetalCLIP) x 1 layer x 1 architecture (TopK) x 1 dictionary size (M=4096) x 1 sparsity (k=16) x 2 poolings (max, mean) x 3 seeds = 6 distinct feature-profile constructions (seeds are a replication filter, not separate constructions).

Control arms are not constructions - they are the denominator: random-weight encoder, spatially-shuffled input, and the 3 other frozen encoders for cross-replication (8c/8d). These are pre-specified and their statistics are reported alongside, never selected among.

Baselines: PCA-64 and ICA-32 = 2 more, fixed component counts, no sweep.

ENDPOINTS. Interpretability (primary): number of replicated features clearing the random-encoder gap; the anatomy/physics split; abstractness entropy distributions. These are DESCRIPTIVE - the multiplicity load sits on the feature-to-variable naming step, and it is handled correctly by construction: the permutation MAX-STATISTIC over all 4096 features already absorbs the within-bank search (bar |r| > 0.145 at n=908, 95th pct; 0.155 at 99th). Outcome-facing (secondary, run ONCE at the end): 5 endpoints - GA, birth percentile, <p10, >p90, PE-as-negative-control.

ADJUSTED BAR. Secondary endpoint tests: 6 constructions x 5 endpoints = 30 tests. Bonferroni at family alpha=0.05 gives per-test alpha=0.00167. Combined with the project's standing >= 2000-resample bootstrap requirement, report 99.8% CIs on secondary outcome associations, not 95%.

PROJECT-LEVEL LOAD. This is family ~16-18 of roughly 15 already tried, so the prior on any positive is low and the bar rises accordingly. Concretely: (i) the SAE-beats-VQ claim needs per-fetus r >= 0.68 against VQ's 0.615, because the paired bootstrap at n=908 cannot resolve a difference below ~0.065; (ii) no result is reported on the strength of one arm - the random-encoder gap must accompany every named feature; (iii) if the M=4096/k=16 grid point fails, the honest report is that it failed. Adding grid points post hoc converts this from a pre-registered test into a search, and if that happens it must be labelled exploratory and the bar re-derived at the new M (the null max |r| table for M=320/1024/4096/16384 is already computed for exactly that purpose).
cost:
GPU: ~3-5 GPU-hours total, comfortably inside the project's stated envelope (3h acceptable, 15h needs justification) - and it can be split into <1h chunks.
- Trained-encoder SAE fits: 3 seeds x 5 folds on 5.2M x 1024 patch rows. A TopK SAE at this scale is minutes to tens of minutes per fit on one GPU node.
- Control arms: the same again for the random-weight arm and the shuffled arm, so 45 fits total (3 arms x 3 seeds x 5 folds).
- One extra extraction pass for the random-weight FetalCLIP over 20,413 frames: the project's measured rate is ~10 min/epoch for FOUR encoders, so well under an hour for one.

No new extraction for the trained encoders: the ~1TB of full-token stores is already on disk, and only one pre-registered layer is read.
CPU: naming statistics, permutation max-statistics (>= 2000 fetus-level permutations), paired bootstraps, PCA/ICA baselines - minutes to low hours.
Storage: 4096-d sparse codes at k=16 over 5.2M patches stored as (index, value) pairs is ~0.7GB per arm per seed; keep only the per-frame pooled profiles (20,413 x 4096 dense float16 ~= 170MB per arm) plus top-patch indices.
HUMAN time is the real bottleneck: step 11 requires a domain expert to look at top-patch panels for every replicated feature. Budget one focused session per ~30 features. This is also where the track's value is created, so it should not be compressed.
inputs_already_on_disk: FetalCLIP ViT-L/14 patch tokens, 20,413 IMPACT frames / 908 fetuses, 256 patches/frame, 1024-d = 5.2M patch rows. No re-extraction of the trained encoder needed; only the random-weight arm needs a new pass.
